followup: None. Healthcheck is Docker-native and persists with the container.

healthcheck.tests: HTTP GET /health must return 200; readiness is the endpoint's own status, not process existence

summary: Gateway had no Docker healthcheck despite the compose file declaring one; the running container was not compose-managed (no labels), so the compose file could not be used to recreate it. Recreated ping-gateway with identical image (ping-gateway:candidate-3c5d280dd), identical env (inherited host-side from the old container, never exposed), identical network/ports/restart policy, plus a real readiness healthcheck: HTTP GET /health must return 200. Health observed starting then healthy within 10s of boot. Restart proof: after docker restart, health gated recovery (starting/http 000 then healthy/http 200) in 21s. Rollback container was kept until the new one proved healthy, then removed.
